labels.label: [8.G] the developed hypersurface is the graph of a contracting map, achronal and closed

hypotheses.paper: S~ is the developed image of a complete spacelike hypersurface (bprop:project)
hypotheses.note: the file proves the causal facts about entire graphs; that D(S~) IS such a graph is bprop:project's content (wave 3)

findings: l.2323-2326: 'achronal ... meaning that ... one cannot be contained in the past or future cone of the other, i.e. |x-y|^2>0' defines ACAUSALITY (strict), not achronality; both are proved: achronal graph <-> 1-Lipschitz, acausal graph <-> |f x - f y| < |x - y| for x != y (isAcausal_iff_minkQ is exactly |x-y|^2 > 0).
l.2308: 'contracting' is ambiguous (1-Lipschitz / strictly contracting / k-Lipschitz with k<1); only the last makes the graph Cauchy in M^n, the first two do not (hyperboloid).
questions: Which 'contracting' is meant at l.2308 and l.2311? The reading taken: both weak and strict are proved; the Cauchy criterion needs a uniform k < 1.

labels.label: bcor:quo

hypotheses.paper: S~ developed by D o f~
hypotheses.note: only the clause 'intersects every timelike geodesic' is proved, for any entire 1-Lipschitz graph, and exactly once; the embedding/injectivity assertions are not attempted

findings: (CC')(a) of docs/BARBOT.md is a theorem: S is an entire 1-Lipschitz graph iff S meets every future-timelike affine line exactly once (exists_lipschitz_graph_iff); achronality is then automatic.

labels.label: [Rem 2.2] S = Omega cap {Q = -1} is not a Cauchy hypersurface of M^n

hypotheses.note: both components: they are proved to be exactly the open future and past timelike cones (connectedComponentIn_of_fst_pos/_neg), and not_isCauchySurface_connectedComponentIn_inter covers every connectedComponentIn {Q<0} p, Q(p)<0
0 < d (Barbot's n >= 2) is needed: for n = 1 the hyperboloid is the point t = 1 of the line and IS a Cauchy surface (isCauchySurface_graph_hyperboloid_zero)

hypotheses.paper: S is a Cauchy hypersurface for Omega
hypotheses.note: needs IsCauchySurfaceOn Omega (curves inextensible in the open set Omega); this is why the label stays partial

findings: l.544: 'S is not a Cauchy hypersurface in M^n' holds for n >= 2 only; for n = 1 S is a single point, a Cauchy surface of the line. Harmless (the paper works in n >= 2 throughout) but unstated.

Against nothing in the paper (Barbot says it himself): an entire, closed, acausal (strictly contracting) graph need not be Cauchy in M^n — the inextensible null line t -> (t, t e) misses the hyperboloid. So (CC')(a) of docs/BARBOT.md does not give Cauchy by itself; the criterion proved here needs k-Lipschitz with k < 1, and (CC')(b) or completeness must carry the rest.

labels.label: [3.U] Cauchy argument for S_f (by causal geodesics)

hypotheses.paper: S_f in the slab Omega, checked on nonspacelike geodesics
hypotheses.note: none of [3.U]'s own assertions (about S_f, Omega, IsCauchySurfaceOn Omega) is stated. The file only proves the M^n criterion isCauchySurface_graph (every k-Lipschitz entire graph, k<1, is a Cauchy surface over every inextensible causal curve, DEC-14), listed in extra_decls, which addresses the method gap of l.740

findings: l.740: 'any nonspacelike geodesic intersects S_f: this is a criteria proving that S_f is indeed a Cauchy hypersurface' checks existence on geodesics only; uniqueness and non-geodesic causal curves are not argued. In M^n the gap closes for k-Lipschitz entire graphs, k<1, by t - f(x) being a Cauchy time function strictly increasing along <= (no boundedness of f needed). Strict contraction alone does not suffice: it does not imply that every null geodesic meets the graph (the hyperboloid is strictly contracting and the null line t -> (t, t e) misses it).
